title: Rating Manual: Short-Hold Vehicle Deletions on the Cardinal Personal Auto Policy
content:
When a vehicle comes off a Cardinal Personal Auto Policy, its vehicle removal credit is taken at a short-hold share that follows how long the vehicle was on the schedule.

## Rule

The holding period is counted in calendar days from the effective date of the vehicle's addition to the effective date of the removal, both read from the policy's transaction history. The addition is the vehicle's latest addition entry by effective date.

| Days on the schedule | Short-hold share |
|---|---|
| Fewer than 90 | Three quarters (0.75) |
| 90 or more but fewer than 180 | Nine tenths (0.9) |
| 180 or more | One |

## Boundaries (hypothetical)

| Addition effective | Removal effective | Days | Share |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 January 2026 | 31 March 2026 | 89 | 0.75 |
| 1 January 2026 | 1 April 2026 | 90 | 0.9 |
| 1 January 2026 | 29 June 2026 | 179 | 0.9 |
| 1 January 2026 | 30 June 2026 | 180 | One |

## Worked illustration (hypothetical)

For a hypothetical credit base of 240.00, a vehicle held 89 days is credited at three quarters, which is 180.00. A vehicle held 120 days is credited at nine tenths, which is 216.00. A vehicle held 200 days is credited at one, the full 240.00.
